about: The access that Meternaut needs outside its own resource group. Meternaut holds no write right: every grant below only reads, and a change to Azure is made with the token of the person who approved it, so that Azure checks that person's own rights (docs/proposals/03-access-and-onboarding.md). The deployment workflow's identity holds no right there and must not get one (AGENTS.md rule 18), so a person who may assign roles at each place grants it. Each line of grants is one role of one identity at one place. An identity is what a function app runs as, and the principals that hold its grants are listed as its holders: the app's own system-assigned identity, found on the app with the option that siteOption names. While an app is moved between kinds of identity, both kinds are holders (a user-assigned one has a name), so that the app is never without access. The list retired records what an earlier version granted and must now be removed: either a custom role that is no longer wanted at all (every assignment of it, then the role), or, with replacedBy, a grant of an identity that an app no longer runs as (only that identity's own assignment: the role stays, because the grant that replaces it needs it), or, with roleStays, a grant of a built-in role that nothing needs any more (only the own assignment of the identities that the item names, never anybody else's: the role is built in and stays). tools/access-requirements.py reads this file: it checks what is granted, grants what is missing only with --apply, and with retire removes what is retired, again only with --apply. On 2026-11-07 the owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to his API Management instance: the cases app reads no key any more, so the custom role that read one (W7) and its grant are retired, and retire removes every assignment of that role at the instance's resource group and below it, then the role. The deployment identity's own custom role in that group (W8) is retired the same way, because no Hub action uses it since the actions that made objects on the instance were removed. The same day the owner ordered the usage recording removed, because nothing fed it any more: the usage app read the old gateway's telemetry, so its two reads (Monitoring Reader on the gateway's Application Insights, and a custom role on the central workspace that read one table) are retired as W9 and W10, and the Hub action retire-old deletes the usage app. Run retire for W9 before that action, while the usage app and its identity still exist, because an assignment of a deleted identity cannot be traced to it. On 2026-11-07 the owner ordered that the Watch watch the entire estate: the cases app reads every subscription that its identity can read, so R1 and R2 are given once, by a person and outside the template, at the tenant root management group (or at each subscription, to watch only those); this file and the template give nothing there. docs/proposals/03-access-and-onboarding.md shows the two tables that the tool prints, and a test keeps them the same.

places.estate: The estate that the Watch reads: the tenant root management group (the Watch then reads every subscription that its identity can read: the app setting SCOPE_ALL_SUBSCRIPTIONS), or each subscription one by one (the app setting SCOPE_SUBSCRIPTIONS, which is also the fallback)
places.gatewayInsights: The old gateway's Application Insights component
places.gatewayGroup: The resource group of the owner's API Management instance, and everything below it
places.centralWorkspace: The central workspace that the component writes to, and the resource group that holds it
places.projectGroup: The project's own resource group, where Meternaut plants waste of its own

grants.why: Reads the list of the subscriptions that the identity can read (the Watch reads every one of them), their resources, tags and management locks, Azure Advisor's cost recommendations, the platform metrics that Azure Monitor keeps for a resource and the pricing settings of the Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans: the detectors, the guards and the read-only tools of the investigator. It also reads a managed disk or a public IP address of the project's own resource group when the timer checks that a deleted resource is gone. A person gives it at the tenant root management group or each subscription: at the group the Watch reads the entire estate, at a subscription only that one. The role reads and changes nothing

Reads the cost lines of every resource for the last 30 days, so that every figure is Cost Management's and never a model's. A person gives it at the tenant root management group or each subscription, with R1; without it a subscription is still read, and the History says that its cost lines could not be read

retired.why: The writer of an earlier version: a custom role that read and deleted a managed disk and a public IP address in this group, held by this identity. Meternaut holds no write right now: a change is made with the token of the person who approved it, and Azure checks that person's own rights. The role's assignments and the role are removed with retire; the identity is removed by the deployment workflow or by the owner
Held by the user-assigned identity that the cases app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R1). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the role stays: R1 needs it
Held by the user-assigned identity that the cases app ran as before its own system-assigned identity took over (R2). Only that identity's assignment is removed, and the role stays: R2 needs it

A custom role of an earlier version that read one key of one subscription of the owner's API Management instance (and nothing else), so that the cases app could call the models through that instance. It was held by the cases app's own system-assigned identity and, before that, by this user-assigned identity. The owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to that instance on 2026-11-07, and the app reads no key any more: it calls the models of its own Foundry project with its own identity. Every assignment of the role at the instance's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself

A custom role of the first environment that the deployment workflow's identity held in the resource group of the owner's API Management instance, so that the Hub could add Citadel's objects to the instance, attach an identity to it and make the access product of the first cases on it. No Hub action uses it since 2026-11-07: the owner ordered the undo of what Meternaut added to that instance, and the actions that made those objects were removed. Every assignment of the role at the instance's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself. The identity stays: it deploys the project's own resource group, and it lives in the bootstrap group, so it is not looked up

The usage app's read of the old gateway's Application Insights component, where the gateway recorded the token metrics of every call, so that the copy jobs of the usage recording could copy them. The owner ordered the usage recording removed on 2026-11-07, because nothing fed it any more: the app is deleted by the Hub action retire-old. The role is built in and stays, because other people hold it. Only the own assignments of the two identities that the usage app ran as are removed: its system-assigned identity, found by reading the app named by --usage-site, and the user-assigned identity id-meternaut-usage that it ran as before. Run this before the Hub action retire-old, while the app and the identity still exist: an assignment of a deleted identity cannot be traced to it

A custom role of the usage recording that read one table (AppMetrics, the metrics of workspace-based Application Insights) of the central workspace, so that its copy jobs could read the gateway's token metrics, and nothing else. It was defined in the resource group of that workspace and held by the usage app's own system-assigned identity and, before that, by the user-assigned identity id-meternaut-usage. Nothing reads those metrics any more (the owner ordered the usage recording removed on 2026-11-07). Every assignment of the role at the workspace's resource group and below it is removed, whoever holds it, and then the role itself
